title: QBR experiment canvas for tiered upgrades and SLA pilots
kpi_targets: Average deal uplift (ARR) from tiered offers >= 27%
SLA add-on attach rate >= 12% in top-20 accounts
content:
Purpose and scope:
Short: an experiment-ready QBR canvas to run A/Bed outreach and technical pilots for customers that are good fits for Dedicated capacity upgrades, Private deployment trials, or premium SLA add-ons. Focus is measurement-first: run small, instrument heavily, iterate.

Context / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis A: Customers with 95th pct latency spikes + steady token growth (>15% qtr) will accept a Dedicated upgrade if presented with a 60-day low-risk pilot and a clear cost-per-token delta.
- Hypothesis B: Regulated customers (finance, health) with activeaudit requests are more likely to convert to Private deployments when shown an end-to-end data flow diagram, KMS integration plan, and a 30-day security validation window.
- Hypothesis C: Premium SLA add-on converts when paired with a reliability scorecard showing historical incidents + a 3-tier remediation SLA mapped to customer pain.

Experiment design (high level):
- Cohorts: pick 30 accounts per cohort (A: high-latency growth; B: compliance flagged; C: strategic enterprise)
- Arms: (1) Control = standard QBR (talk track only), (2) Offer = QBR + tailored upgrade offer + technical pilot, (3) Tech-first = invitation to 30-day private pilot with dedicated engineering touch.
- Randomization: stratify by ARR band and vertical.
- Duration: 60-day measurement window with interim 14/30/45-day check-ins.
- Success metrics: offer acceptance, pilot activation, paid conversion within 90 days, NPS change + cost delta realized.

QBR Canvas (sections to use during meeting):
1) One-line value statement: "Reduce per-request latency and predictable unit-cost while preserving baseline model quality."
2) Observed signals: attach per-route latency p95, token growth, error spikes, recent support tickets referencing rate limits, audit asks.
3) Product recommendation(s): Dedicated baseline / Private trial / SLA add-on (explicit: duration, price delta, infra changes).
4) Business case: side-by-side cost table (current vs projected) + qualitative benefits (SLA credits, dedicated burst capacity).
5) Risk & rollback: list migration steps, fallbacks to hosted, rollback timeline, estimated downtime (usually zero but list caveats).
6) Ask & next steps: pilot start date, technical kickoff owner, procurement contacts, data handling checklist.

Technical prerequisites checklist (to attach):
- IP allowlist / VPC peering info collected (yes/no)
- KMS/HSM key provisioning steps documented
- Model pin/version requested
- Expected TPS and peak concurrency estimate
- Test prompt set for quality regression checks (link or sample)
- Data retention / logging requirements (retention days, export needs)
- Contact: Solutions Eng assigned + SRE point-of-contact

Outreach sequence (example; personalize per account):
- Day -10: Internal prep: gather metrics, recent incident timeline, cost calc (owner: CSM)
- Day 0: QBR meeting (present canvas)
- Day 2: Follow up email with PDF + pilot terms (CSM + SE)
- Day 7: Technical pre-kickoff (if interested)
- Day 14: Pilot activation + weekly status standups
- Day 30: Mid-pilot checkpoint (30-day metrics + red/green flags)
- Day 60: Pilot close + conversion proposal or rollback plan

Pricing & packaging heuristics (guide, not prescriptive):
- Dedicated pilot: 60-day free or heavily discounted reserved pool access for evaluation; conversion based on committed reserved slots or monthly commit.
- Private deployment: 30-day validation fee + onboarding fee; discounted first-year platform fee when convert within 90 days.
- SLA add-on: tiered (Silver/Gold/Platinum) mapping to response/repair times, credits, and dedicated support hours.

Objection handling cheat-sheet (short):
- "We’re not ready to commit capex": offer time-boxed pilot and option to revert to hosted with no data loss.
- "Cost looks higher": show unit economics (tokens/sec) and projected savings from batching/caching + lower error retries.
- "Security concerns": share redacted SOC logs, KMS integration diagram, and propose technical deep-dive with security team.

Measurement & reporting (what to instrument):
- Pilot activation timestamp, pilot traffic fraction, p95 latency delta, per-token compute cost change, request success rate, function-call regressions, customer-reported incidents.
- Weekly pilot dashboard template: single row per account with color-coded flags (green/amber/red) and comments.

Sample tracker snippet (copy into sheet):
- Columns: Account | ARR band | Cohort | Offer type | QBR date | Pilot start | Pilot end | Pilot status | Pilot-to-paid | ARR uplift | Owner | Next action | Notes
- Use conditional formatting for Pilot status and Pilot-to-paid columns.

Rollout playbook for conversion (if pilot passes):
1) Final proposal & procurement timeline (CSM + Finance)
2) SLA contract amendment (Legal)
3) Migration checklist: model pinning, capacity plan, routable endpoints, DNS cutover plan
4) Post-conversion: 30/60/90 day QBR cadence to validate SLOs and cost targets

Open questions / risks to call out (working list):
- Do we need a minimum pilot traffic quota to consider pilot successful? (propose: >2k requests/day for 14 consecutive days)
- Cost recognition vs sales quotas: how do we book discounted pilots? (finance / rev ops to weigh in)
- SE bandwidth: how many concurrent Private pilots can Solutions Eng support? (SRE capacity gating)

Templates to attach (placeholders):
- follow-up email (short)
- pilot terms one-pager (technical + commercial bullets)
- QBR slide deck (talking points)
- pilot dashboard link (sheet id)

Notes to self / next edits:
- Add example cost calc for conversational vs embed-heavy workloads (impact of batching + cache).
- Survey CSMs after 1st run to collect talk-track improvements.
- Coordinate with product to get latest Dedicated burst policy and SLA wording before finalizing pilot terms.

Quick sample follow-up email (editable):
Subject: Next steps from our QBR — Dedicated pilot option\nHi <Name>, thanks again for the QBR today. Attached is a one-pager summarizing the Dedicated pilot we discussed, the technical prerequisites, and a proposed start window. If it looks ok we can schedule a 30-min kickoff with Solutions Engineering to scope network and KMS setup.

Best,
<CSM name>

-- end of canvas --

(rough notes style — use as modular content for QBR binder. This doc should be copied into account-specific QBRs and the data columns in the tracker sheet.)
